title: Ring Neighbors Alert Failure Rate
dataSources: Nextdoor posts (`nextdoor:post`), Ring Neighbors alerts (`ring:neighbor`), neighborhood watch logs (`neighborhood:watch`), and local alerts (`local:alert`).
app: Nextdoor post exports, Ring Neighbors alerts, neighborhood watch logs, and local emergency alert feeds ingested into Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=ring:neighbor
| eval status_value=lower(coalesce(alert_status,"unknown"))
| eval failed=if(match(status_value,"error|fail|alert|overdue|late|stale|breach"),1,0)
| stats count as events, sum(failed) as failed_events by alert_type
| eval failure_pct=round(100*failed_events/events,1)
| sort - failure_pct - failed_events
description: Measures how often Ring Neighbors alert records land in an unhealthy or exception state for each alert type.
value: A plain failure-rate view highlights noisy devices, flaky automations, and habits that repeatedly slip.
implementation: Normalize alert_status values into good or bad states and review the failure percentage per alert type.
visualization: Bar chart of failure percentage by entity.
grandmaExplanation: It highlights which parts of your Ring Neighbors alert data keep ending up in a bad state instead of working cleanly.
